core_obligations: Choose a presentation of M by a free module over the polynomial ring and exhibit finitely many kernel elements that generate the kernel after localising at the chosen primes and at a given prime (proof lines 5801-5812).
Form the quotient M' of the free module by the submodule generated by those elements and show that M' and M agree after localisation at the given prime (proof lines 5812-5816).
Apply openness of flatness to localise at an element so that M' becomes flat over R (proof lines 5816-5818).

Use the displayed commutative diagram, the injectivity hypothesis on the base and the flatness of the two modules to show that the surjection M' to M becomes an isomorphism after localisation, and conclude finite presentation by the cover lemma (proof lines 5818-5830).
proof_roadmap: Present M and choose the kernel generators (proof lines 5801-5812).
Compare M' with M locally at the given prime (proof lines 5812-5816).
Get flatness of M' by openness of flatness (proof lines 5816-5818).
Use the diagram and the cover lemma to conclude (proof lines 5818-5831).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a finite flat module over a polynomial ring is finitely presented as soon as it is finitely presented at finitely many primes which detect the base by the injectivity of the map to the product of localisations, and the proof is a 31-line argument combining openness of flatness with a diagram. It presents the module, finds finitely many elements of the kernel that generate it after localising at the chosen primes and at a given prime of the polynomial ring, forms the resulting quotient module, uses openness of flatness to localise so that this quotient is flat, and then compares the two flat modules through the product of localisations to conclude that the surjection between them is injective. The two inputs that do the work are the openness theorem and the injectivity hypothesis on the base, and both are used explicitly.
